'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Afghanistan–Pakistan clashes (2024–present)|Afghanistan–Pakistan clashes]]
**[[2025 Afghanistan–Pakistan conflict]]
***[[Pakistan]] claims that it killed at least 15 [[Taliban]] members in an [[airstrike]] in [[Spin Boldak]], [[Afghanistan]]. The Taliban claims that twelve civilians are killed and over 100 are injured. Both countries also claim that they killed several soldiers during a [[shootout]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c3dnvnjdg1ro (BBC News)]
***Pakistan carries out two airstrikes against [[Kabul]], capital of Afghanistan. The target and the result are unknown. After the attack, both countries agree to a 48-hour [[ceasefire]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c3dnvnjdg1ro (BBC News)]
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[Gaza war hostage crisis]]
***[[Hamas]] returns two more hostages' bodies to the [[Red Cross]], with 19 still in Gaza despite the [[Gaza peace plan]]'s deadline last Monday. [[Donald Trump]] also states [[Israel]] may resume fighting if he believes Hamas does not uphold their part of the agreement. [https://apnews.com/article/gaza-israel-hamas-hostages-ceasefire-10-15-2025-435b7d15bc971f902d4dda967e4a609a (AP)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Kupiansk offensive]], [[Humanitarian impacts of the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Humanitarian impacts of the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***[[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] authorities order mass evacuations across 40 settlements and towns in northeastern [[Kharkiv Oblast]], citing the worsening situation around the city of [[Kupiansk]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/ukraine-authorities-order-mass-evacuations-around-devastated-kupiansk-2025-10-14/ (Reuters)]
*[[Papua conflict]]
**Fourteen people are killed by [[Indonesian Army|Indonesian soldiers]] during a six-hours battle with [[Free Papua Movement]] [[Separatism|separatists]] in [[Intan Jaya Regency]], [[Central Papua]]. The army claims that all of those killed were militants, while the group claims that nine civilians and three militants are among the dead.  [https://apnews.com/article/indonesia-papua-insurgents-deadly-clash-army-cdd6c3213531be78d81d269f3ecbbd39 (AP)]
*[[Ecuadorian conflict (2024–present)|Ecuadorian conflict]]
**Explosive devices detonate on two bridges in [[Ecuador]]. No casualties are reported. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/explosions-reported-bridges-ecuador-violence-escalates-2025-10-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[Haitian conflict (2020–present)|Haitian conflict]]
**[[Doctors Without Borders]] announce that they are permanently closing their offices in [[Port-au-Prince]], [[Haiti]], due to safety concerns. [https://apnews.com/article/haiti-msf-doctors-without-borders-center-closes-violence-68595071309e258e9c67ca233eb31822 (AP)]
*[[Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]
**Six [[Pakistan Army|Pakistani soldiers]] and nine [[Pakistani Taliban]] gunmen are killed in a [[shootout]] in [[Orakzai District]], [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]], Pakistan. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/over-12-civilians-killed-attacks-afghanistan-by-pakistani-forces-afghan-taliban-2025-10-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[United States–Venezuela relations]], [[2025 US Caribbean naval deployment]], [[United States involvement in regime change in Latin America]]
**The [[United States]] reportedly greenlights covert operations in [[Venezuela]] targeting [[President of Venezuela|president]] [[Nicolás Maduro]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2025/10/15/us/politics/trump-covert-cia-action-venezuela.html (''The New York Times'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Ten people are killed and 21 others are injured, including four critically, in an explosion on a [[crude oil|crude]] [[palm oil]] [[oil tanker|tanker]] docked at a [[shipyard]] on [[Batam Island]], [[Indonesia]]. [https://apnews.com/article/indonesia-tanker-fire-crude-palm-oil-b2d9fc97bde7df3b9454553a52fb8549 (AP)] [https://www.marineinsight.com/shipping-news/oil-tanker-explosion-at-indonesias-batam-shipyard-kills-10-injures-over-20/ (Marine Insight)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Cambodia–South Korea relations]], [[Scam centers in Cambodia]]
**[[South Korea]] issues a blanket [[travel ban]] on its citizens to parts of [[Cambodia]] known for its [[scam center]]s, alleging that over 200,000 foreign nationals are working in these centers, including 1,200 [[South Koreans]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/south-korea-bans-travel-to-cambodia-over-scam-centers/a-74368895 (DW)] [https://www.scmp.com/week-asia/people/article/3329091/south-korean-victims-cambodias-scam-camps-recount-horrific-experiences (''South China Morning Post'')]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]], [[Russia–United Kingdom relations]], [[International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**The [[United Kingdom]] imposes new sanctions on [[Russia]]n major energy companies [[Lukoil]] and [[Rosneft]]. [https://newsukraine.rbc.ua/news/uk-imposes-new-sanctions-on-russia-targeting-1760535337.html (RBC-Ukraine)] 

'''Law and crime'''
*[[International Criminal Court investigation in the Philippines]] 
**Judges at the [[International Criminal Court]] dismiss [[Karim Ahmad Khan|Karim Khan]], the [[chief prosecutor]] in the case against former [[President of the Philippines|Philippine president]] [[Rodrigo Duterte]], due to links between Khan and some victims of Duterte's alleged crimes, whom Khan represented prior to [[Arrest of Rodrigo Duterte|Duterte's arrest]]. [https://apnews.com/article/duterte-icc-khan-disqualified-prosecutor-7a80020e7c789d5094f5560568992824 (AP)]
*[[Nord Stream pipelines sabotage]], [[Italy–Ukraine relations]], [[Germany–Italy relations]]
**[[Italy]]'s [[Supreme Court of Cassation (Italy)|Supreme Court of Cassation]] blocks the [[extradition]] of a [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] national suspected of causing explosions which damaged the [[Nord Stream]] [[pipeline]]s in 2022 to [[Germany]], where he is wanted. [https://www.dw.com/en/italy-top-court-blocks-nord-stream-suspect-extradition/a-74360761 (DW)]
*[[Iraq]]i politician Safaa Al Mashhadani, a candidate for the upcoming [[2025 Iraqi parliamentary election|parliamentary elections]], is [[Assassination|assassinated]] by a [[Improvised explosive device|bomb]] attached to his [[car bomb|vehicle]] in [[Al-Tarmia District]]. The perpetrators are unknown. [https://gulfnews.com/world/mena/iraqi-parliamentary-candidate-killed-in-baghdad-car-bombing-1.500308163 (Gulf News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Abortion in Costa Rica]], [[Women's rights in Costa Rica]] 
**[[President of Costa Rica|President]] [[Rodrigo Chaves Robles]] restricts [[abortion]] in [[Costa Rica]] only to cases where the life of the mother is at risk. [https://apnews.com/article/costa-rica-chaves-abortion-2b9efaccd086a9ca3086b728d0907a80 (AP)]
*[[Euthanasia in Uruguay]]
**[[Uruguay]] becomes the first country in [[Latin America]] to decriminalise [[euthanasia]] via legislation after the law is passed by the [[Senate of Uruguay|Senate]]. [https://apnews.com/article/uruguay-euthanasia-law-076a2f4d2ba5ce990e65ac4dd4798d49 (AP)]
*[[Guatemala]]n [[President of Guatemala|president]] [[Bernardo Arévalo]] accepts the resignation of three top security officials following a jailbreak where 20 members of the [[18th Street gang|Barrio 18]] gang escaped from prison. [https://apnews.com/article/guatemala-barrio-18-gang-prison-escape-5e92fec5ad918247ad243826a3ed5937 (AP)]
